So, for most of human history, the Middle East has been the wealthiest part of the world. The Levant, especially Jerusalem, is at the center of the world because it connects all major civilizations—Egypt, Anatolia, Mesopotamia, and the Persians. Over here is the Mediterranean. As you can see, basically all roads lead to Jerusalem, which means whoever controls Jerusalem controls the major trade access point. This makes Jerusalem a highly profitable part of any empire.

For these empires, keeping Jerusalem under control has always been problematic because whoever controls it can switch sides. If Mesopotamia controls Jerusalem, Egypt might bribe it to change allegiances. Various techniques were employed to control Jerusalem. The Babylonians tried taking captives as hostages but this didn't work well. So, the Babylonians destroyed Jerusalem. This splintered and scattered the Israeli identity.

Eventually, the Babylonians were conquered by the Persians who adopted a divide and rule strategy. They created a Jewish identity in Jerusalem, leading to conflict with the locals. Jews are not forever loyal to Persia because they see themselves as foreigners within the Levant. By swearing loyalty to Persia, Jews gain control over the Levant, but in return, Persia finances the construction of their second temple.

A Jewish identity emerged with three key pillars: monotheism (believing Yahweh is the only God and being the chosen people due to a covenant with Abraham), following the law of Moses (including the Torah and oral traditions like the ten commandments), and using the Bible as collective memory. The first major characteristic is that Jerusalem and the second temple become the center of worship for Jews, who must make animal sacrifices and adhere to strict laws governing behavior.

Over time, Jewish people spread across the world, working as mercenaries in Persian armies, moving to the Hellenic world for economic opportunities. This led to a merging of Jewish, Greek, and Persian cultures, giving birth to Western civilization.
